title: DST Placement Coordination
name: DST Placement Coordination
metaTitle: DST Placement Coordination in Fort Worth, TX
metaDescription: Fort Worth 1031 exchange DST placement coordination: matching exchange proceeds to Delaware statutory trust replacement interests within the 45-day window.

sections.html: A Delaware statutory trust interest can qualify as like-kind replacement property in a 1031 exchange under published IRS guidance, giving Fort Worth investors an option when a direct-title replacement is not available within the 45-day window. Placement coordination covers matching exchange proceeds to a specific DST offering, documenting the interest correctly, and closing before the 180-day deadline.

sections.heading: Why Investors Consider a DST Placement
sections.html:
Investors exchanging out of a Cultural District retail building or a Near Southside multifamily property sometimes reach the 45-day mark without a direct replacement under contract. A DST interest in institutional-grade real estate, often outside the Fort Worth market entirely, can be identified and closed within the remaining window because the offering is already structured and diligenced ahead of time.

Placement coordination also comes into play when an investor wants to reduce management responsibility after selling an actively managed local asset, since DST interests are passive by structure.

sections.heading: Matching Proceeds to a Compliant Offering
sections.html:
Not every DST offering is structured to preserve exchange eligibility; the trust document has to meet the requirements set out under the applicable revenue ruling, including restrictions on the trustee's ability to renegotiate loans or raise new capital. Confirming an offering's structure before identification, rather than after, prevents a last-minute disqualification.

  • Confirm the DST sponsor's offering meets exchange-eligible trust requirements
  • Match the exchange proceeds amount to the required minimum investment
  • Verify the identification notice describes the specific DST interest
  • Coordinate closing timing with the sponsor's subscription deadlines

sections.heading: Identification and Closing Mechanics
sections.html: A DST interest is identified the same way as any other replacement property, by written notice with a specific description delivered to the qualified intermediary before day 45. Closing then follows the sponsor's subscription process rather than a traditional purchase contract, which changes the document set but not the underlying 180-day deadline.

sections.heading: Coordinating With the Qualified Intermediary and Tax Advisor
sections.html: Because DST placements involve fractional ownership interests rather than direct title, the qualified intermediary and the investor's tax advisor are both looped in early to confirm the proceeds transfer mechanics and to document the exchange correctly for later reporting.

sections.heading: Evaluating Multiple DST Offerings Side by Side
sections.html:
Investors weighing more than one DST offering as a fallback for a Near Southside or Alliance-area sale typically compare each sponsor's offering memorandum against the same set of criteria: property type, leverage level, holding period expectations, and the sponsor's track record with prior offerings. Because these interests are illiquid for the duration of the trust's holding period, that comparison happens before proceeds are committed, not after.

Coordination at this stage also includes confirming subscription capacity, since a popular offering can fill before an investor's exchange proceeds are ready to fund, which is why preflight conversations with a sponsor typically start well before the 45-day identification deadline rather than in its final days.

Investors also compare the fee structure across offerings, since acquisition fees, asset management fees, and disposition fees vary by sponsor and directly affect net returns over the trust's holding period. A side-by-side comparison table covering property type, leverage, projected hold period, and full fee schedule for each offering under consideration gives an investor exchanging out of a Fort Worth-area asset a clearer basis for the decision than reviewing each offering memorandum in isolation.

Sponsor track record deserves particular attention, since a DST program is only as reliable as the sponsor's history of returning capital and managing the underlying assets through a full holding period. Reviewing a sponsor's prior offerings, including how earlier funds performed relative to their initial projections, gives an investor a more grounded basis for comparison than the current offering memorandum alone.

Because a DST interest is generally illiquid until the trust disposes of the underlying property, coordination also includes setting realistic expectations about the holding period at the outset. An investor moving out of an actively managed Fort Worth property into a passive DST interest should understand the projected hold period before committing proceeds, since an early exit is typically not available the way it might be with directly held real estate.

faqs.q: Can a Fort Worth investor identify a DST interest alongside a direct property on the same list?
faqs.a: Yes. A DST interest can be listed as one of several identified candidates under the three-property, 200%, or 95% rule, giving the investor optionality if a direct replacement falls through.

faqs.q: Does a DST placement require the investor to manage the underlying property?
faqs.a: No. DST interests are passive by structure, with the trustee handling management, which is part of why investors selling an actively managed Fort Worth building sometimes consider this option.

faqs.q: Is every DST offering automatically eligible for 1031 exchange treatment?
faqs.a: No. Only offerings structured to meet specific trust requirements under IRS guidance qualify, so the offering documents need review before an investor relies on it as replacement property.

faqs.q: What happens if the exchange proceeds do not exactly match the DST minimum investment?
faqs.a: Sponsors typically set minimum investment amounts, and any proceeds above that minimum may need to be allocated elsewhere or discussed with the sponsor, since a mismatch can leave a portion of proceeds unplaced.

faqs.q: Should a tax advisor be involved before selecting a DST placement?
faqs.a: Yes. Given the fractional-interest structure and sponsor-specific terms, a tax advisor should review the offering and its fit with the investor's overall exchange before funds are committed.
